notebook:

note: Prune the low-value light branch and concentrate duty on the two high-value C5/C6 blend products.
notebook:

Current five-column plant costs $910M/yr and sells nothing. The light blends are worth only ~$160M/yr versus >$150M/yr extra columns, so T is pruned. BTB is already 93% C6 paraffin ($613M/yr potential), and BTT can become a ~$614M/yr C5 blend if B makes a sharp N-pentane/DMB split. Testing 110 stages/R=10 at B and 90/R=8 at BT. Root remains 80/R=8/dp=.05 for now; later optimize its costly settings.

note: Test whether higher column pressures materially cut refrigeration and energy costs while retaining the saleable C6 blend.
notebook:

Higher pressure drop should reduce cold-condenser penalties and duties; test dp .30/.25/.20 before changing the separation structure. Agent-2 confirms low-pressure roots are extremely costly and more small columns do not pay.

note: Use a small BTT finishing column to remove its 15% N-pentane contamination, allowing substantial duty reductions in the expensive full-feed columns.
notebook:

Current root is a very expensive mixed light/heavy split; avoid further tall/high-reflux feed columns. Agent-2's seven-column plants remain negative, confirming small downstream columns are preferable but extra low-value branches do not pay.

note: Add a small finishing splitter on BTTT to recover its valuable C5 blend, which is currently unsold only because of heavy C6 contamination.
notebook:

notebook:
